tone_statements.citation: Mortensen, David. 2003. Review of Baheng-yu yanjiu 巴哼语研究 [Research on the Pahng language], by Mao Zongwu and Li Yunbing (Shanghai: Shanghai Far East Publishers, 1997, 344 pp.). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 26(1): 123-131. doi:10.32655/ltba.26.1.07
tone_statements.quote: The section on Hmnai also gives examples of tone sandhi, illustrating an interesting pattern where native words show anticipatory tone sandhi, but modern loan-words from Chinese show perseveratory tone sandhi patterns (13-14). Unfortunately, there is little or no discussion of tone sandhi in Pahng proper, so that it is not quite clear whether the sample dialects even feature tone sandhi, and if they do, what tone sandhi is like in these languages.
tone_statements.summary: Hm Nai (Huxingshan) is tonal with tone sandhi (anticipatory in native words, perseveratory in recent Chinese loans) per Mao & Li 1997:13-14; inventory not given in the review (zh.wikipedia, citing Mao & Li 1997:98, says Wunai shares Pa-Hng's 8 tone categories/values).

tone_statements.citation: Strecker, David. 1987. Some comments on Benedict's "Miao-Yao enigma: the Na-e language". Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 10(2): 22-42.
tone_statements.quote: Compare Hm Nai [lian 6] (tone C2) (Mao and Meng 1982:78) and 18th century "Yao" of northwest Hunan liang (Lombard- Salmon 1972 7316) 6 I suspect that the "Yao" vocabulary repro- duced by Lombard-Salmon belongs to the Hm Nai group rather than to the West Hunan branch of Hmongic as Benedict suggests. Benedict's Chinese etymology for these words for ‘dog' is very plausible, although there is the problem of the tonal dis- agreement: Chinese A2 versus Hm Nai C2 versus Pa Hng Dl.
tone_statements.summary: Hm Nai treated as a tonal Hmong-Mien language with the A/B/C/D x register (1-8) category system; categories cited per word, inventory not stated in pp.1-12.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 613 (hdl:1885/146760, CC-BY).
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Comparative work; a full-text search for stress/accent Wunai / Hm Nai / Ng Nai / Longhui / 唔奈 gives zero hits, so Wunai is not among its data points. Only stress remarks are general (iambic weak-strong prefix+root pattern in Hmong-Mien, p. ~the text; loanword stress in Thai). Nothing on Wunai stress.
